author: reek
body: It had no arm in the emitter's binary-operator dispatch and fell through to the catch-all, which returns `reg-rax` having emitted nothing. So `^` answered whatever was in that register: `2 ^ 3` gave 1130508, a code address, and did so for every program this compiler has ever built. The `__ipow` helper was emitted into every binary and never called once.

author: reek
body: Nothing in the tree used the operator, which is why no test and no battery could have noticed. It is documented in the operator table in `docs/DevelopersGuide.md` all the same.

author: reek
body: The exponents here cover the helper's three paths. A zero exponent answers 1; a negative exponent answers 0, which is deliberate rather than accidental -- `emit-ipow` patches that branch to its own `li rax, 0` and returns, which is the truncation of a reciprocal toward zero and agrees with what integer division does; and the square-and-multiply loop handles the rest. The odd and even exponents matter separately because the loop only multiplies the accumulator on a set low bit.

author: reek
body: The negative-exponent answer is not stated in `docs/DevelopersGuide.md`'s operator table. It is pinned here as the behaviour the implementation deliberately has, not as a semantic this test is choosing.
